topSignals.title: Bloom Energy says the first fuel-cell power block is "ready for customer use" at Nebius's 328 MW Vineland, NJ AI data center — but capacity of that first block is undisclosed, and the site itself is not yet operational.
topSignals.text: On Bloom's October 22 Q3 2026 earnings call, CEO KR Sridhar told analysts the first power block for Nebius's New Jersey site was ready; when analyst Christopher Dendrinos asked for a megawatt figure for that block specifically, Sridhar did not give one. The only disclosed numbers remain the contract totals: ~328 MW installed capacity with a 250 MW supply guarantee (a 78 MW/~24% gap between installed and guaranteed), signed May 14, 2026, under a three-phase, 10-year supply structure with aggregate service fees of up to $2.6B over the term. Bloom's own cadence (three months to planning approval, two months more to initial power readiness) implies roughly five months from signing to this first-block milestone, which lines up with the October date. Separately, Nebius itself has not announced the data center as operational — Blockspace reported Oct 23 that the site was still offline. This is a genuine execution milestone (first hardware energized) but not yet a revenue or load-bearing milestone, and it leaves the actual deployed SOFC capacity unquantified — a gap worth flagging for the LCOE model's capacity-factor and revenue-timing assumptions on this project. Note for the archive: prior entries in this monitor have carried this deal as "Bloom/Nebius $2.6B/328 MW (Finland) plus [a separate] Vineland NJ [deal]" — today's reporting (Nebius's own original release named no site; subsequent press has consistently identified the 328 MW/$2.6B project as the Vineland, NJ site itself) suggests these may be the same deal, not two separate ones. Flagged for review rather than silently corrected. TS2.tech | ad-hoc-news.de, Oct 27 | Nebius press release

Competitor roster: SOFC systems for data centers

Bloom Energy: Deployed/signed at multiple named sites — Oracle/Project Jupiter (NM, installation underway, footprint still largely unbuilt, hearing Dec 7), AEP (1 GW), Brookfield EaaS, Nebius (328 MW/$2.6B, Vineland NJ — first fuel-cell power block reported ready for customer use Oct 22, 2026; block capacity undisclosed; data center itself not yet operational), Equinix (>100 MW/19 sites), Aligned "Project Phoenix" (2 GW, PA), Hitachi (Japan), SK Eternix (Icheon/Paju, Korea, 28 MW, operational).

FuelCell Energy (incl. HyAxiom-branded products): Signed orders/PPAs — Fit Energy (up to 380 MW), Inuverse Korea (up to 100 MW), 75 MW Texas Capacity Reservation Agreement, SDCL (up to 450 MW). No named deployment live yet.

Doosan Fuel Cell/HyAxiom: Signed order — US AI data center supply contract (KRW 823.6B cumulative, mixed SOFC/PAFC); separately supplies SOFC stacks to Reverion. No named data-center site of its own yet.
Convion: Pipeline-only/pre-commercial under HD Hyundai ownership; no named data-center customer.
SK ecoplant: Pipeline-only (2023-vintage GDS Singapore SOFC deal); no new named data-center deployment.
Ceres Power's SOFC licensees (Doosan, Delta Electronics, Weichai): Licensing/pipeline-only; no named data-center deployment via Ceres licensing directly.
Reverion: Pipeline-only — Doosan-supplied SOFC stacks for rSOC power plants (Germany); no named data-center customer yet.
Petra Power: Pre-commercial, no named customer; first infrastructure deployment targeted 2028.

lcoe.text: Carry-forward, unchanged:* Virginia data-center electricity tax ($0.011/kWh); PJM Reliability Backstop ceiling (~$202.6/kW-year avoided-cost benchmark, filing suspended pending Feb 28, 2027 paper hearing); PJM's proposed 50 MW behind-the-meter netting threshold (pending FERC approval, 3-year grandfather); FCEL Torrington capex ($200-275M for 350-500 MW/yr by 2028); AEP/Bloom bundled utility-purchase benchmark ($2,944/kW capital+service); Germany's Netzpaket redispatch-curtailment risk (18-20% uncompensated annual-output exposure) for non-islanded SOFC deployments.

Pending calendar (updated):* Project Jupiter dismissal-motion ruling (hearing held Oct 26, outcome still not public), discovery hearing Oct 29 (1 day out), full hearing Dec 7; German Netzpaket/EEG 2027 Bundestag second/third reading targeted for the week of Nov 9-13, Bundesrat Nov 20; German KWK-Gesetz cabinet consideration remains undated past its Oct 14 target; FCEL lead-plaintiff deadline Nov 10 (13 days out); PJM backstop paper hearing runs to Feb 28, 2027; next EIA STEO Nov 10, 2026.
